pages.title: datetime -- Basic date and time types
pages.content: datetime.strptime(date_string, format) parses a string into a datetime object using an explicit format code, for example %d/%m/%Y or %B %d, %Y. It raises ValueError when the string does not match. datetime.date.isoformat() returns the date as YYYY-MM-DD. Both are in the standard library, so no installation is required.

pages.title: Format codes reference
pages.content: Common codes: %Y four digit year, %y two digit year, %m zero padded month, %B full month name, %b abbreviated month name, %d zero padded day. Parsing several different layouts usually means trying a list of candidate formats in order and keeping the first that succeeds.

pages.title: dateutil.parser -- generic date parsing
pages.content: dateutil.parser.parse accepts most human readable date formats without being told the layout. It is a third party package and must be installed with pip before it can be imported. Ambiguous day/month order is resolved with the dayfirst argument.

pages.title: Arrow: better dates and times for Python
pages.content: Arrow is a third party library offering a friendlier API over datetime, with humanized output and timezone conversion. Like dateutil it must be installed from PyPI and is not part of the standard library.

pages.title: PEP 495 -- Local time disambiguation
pages.content: Describes the fold attribute used to disambiguate local times that occur twice because of a daylight saving transition. Relevant to timezone aware parsing, not to parsing date only strings.
